Lasagna gardening! I'm doing it this fall. Basically start a compost pile where you plan on gardening next year. No need to dig. Just pile some straw, chicken poop, grass, leaves, etc and let sit for a few months.

You can also look into Hugelkultur. The reason I think this will be good for you is that it not only 'creates' good soil, it also gives you a good reservoir of water-retentive material underground.

  1. Dig a ditch in your soil, any depth is good but at least 18 inches.
  2. Fill it with woody matter. Tree stumps, logs, etc. Start by laying out the largest pieces. Then fill in the gaps with smaller pieces.
  3. Add twigs, dried leaves, yard waste, etc. Let it all fill up the gaps in your woodpile.
  4. Keep building up (lasagna garden style) until it forms a nice mound, about 2 to 3 feet tall above the ground.

If you top off the mound with some compost and soil, you can plant on the hugel-mound right away - however, for the first year, it would have to be plants which do okay in poor soil. It takes a little while for the decomposition to set in.

The wood under the ground decomposes over time into spongy matter that holds on to water very effectively. The other organic matter decomposes into nutrients, and you end up with about 2 to 3 feet deep bed of nutrient rich, well draining, moisture-retentive soil for years.
